definition: OCLC Connexion is a cataloging tool for creating, editing and sharing bibliographic records through WorldCat.
example: A cataloger updates the description of a book and records that the library holds it.

definition: OCUnit was a unit-testing framework for Objective-C applications, distributed as part of older Apple development tooling.
example: A developer used an OCUnit test to check that a parser handled an empty input.
sense_note: Distinguish it from its later successor XCTest.

definition: Office 365 is Microsoft's subscription service combining Office productivity tools with online services for work and collaboration.
example: A team edits a presentation stored in shared online storage.
sense_note: The label also appears in current and historical subscription names; verify plan-specific inclusions separately.

definition: Office and productivity software supports common work tasks such as editing documents, organizing data, preparing presentations and communicating.
example: An office coordinator builds a spreadsheet to track upcoming deadlines.

definition: omniORB is an implementation of CORBA that lets software components invoke operations across process or network boundaries.
example: A client uses a generated interface to call a service running in another process.

definition: ON1 refers to photography software for organizing, developing and editing digital photographs.
example: A photographer adjusts exposure in a raw file and saves an edited copy.
sense_note: The label names a product family, not an exact edition or feature set.

definition: Onboarding helps a new employee, customer or other participant learn procedures and gain the access and information needed to begin.
example: A manager introduces a new employee to team responsibilities and schedules required training.
sense_note: The target population depends on context.

definition: Oncology sales involves presenting oncology-related products and services to relevant customers within applicable clinical, commercial and compliance boundaries.
example: A representative discusses an approved cancer-care product and its ordering process with a clinic.

definition: OneTrust provides software for managing work such as privacy compliance, consent and governance, risk and compliance.
example: A privacy team tracks requests to access personal information and their resolution status.

definition: Online demonstration presents and explains a product, process or technique to remote viewers using digital tools.
example: A trainer shares a screen and shows a participant how to complete a form.

definition: Onshape is a cloud-based computer-aided design and product data management system for collaborative mechanical design.
example: Two designers review changes to the same assembly and compare design versions.

definition: Open Shortest Path First is a link-state routing protocol for finding routes within an Internet Protocol routing domain.
example: Routers exchange topology information and compute routes using their configured link costs.

definition: The OpenAPI Specification defines a machine-readable format for describing HTTP APIs, including operations, inputs and responses.
example: A team publishes an OpenAPI document to generate client reference documentation.

definition: OpenCart is an e-commerce platform for operating an online store with catalogs, carts, orders and extensions.
example: A merchant creates product pages and tracks incoming orders through its administration interface.

definition: OpenDaylight is an open-source platform for building software-defined network controllers and programmable networking applications.
example: A network operator uses its controller to maintain a topology view of managed devices.

definition: OpenNI is a framework that provides interfaces for sensors and software used in depth sensing and natural interaction.
example: An application reads depth measurements from a supported sensor using its common interface.
sense_note: Hardware and software support vary by version and distribution.

definition: OpenStreetMap is a collaborative geographic database that contributors can edit and users can reuse under its license.
example: A community mapper adds a missing footpath so it appears in downstream maps.

definition: OpenTok is technology for building real-time video and audio communications into applications.
example: A developer adds a video consultation room to an appointment service.
sense_note: The label may occur as a legacy brand; verify applicable product documentation.

definition: OpenTSDB is an open-source database system for storing and querying large volumes of time-series measurements.
example: An operations team queries a week of server utilization measurements by host.

definition: Operational risk mitigation identifies and reduces potential losses arising from failures in people, processes, systems or external events.
example: A finance team adds independent approval to a payment workflow to reduce processing errors.

definition: Operationalizing AI moves an AI system into sustained use with deployment, monitoring, governance and maintenance processes.
example: A team sets up model monitoring and a fallback workflow before releasing an automated classifier.

definition: Operations analytics analyzes operational data to understand performance and make decisions about processes, resources or service delivery.
example: A warehouse analyst identifies which picking steps contribute most to delays.

definition: Ophthalmic surgical assisting supports eye surgery by preparing equipment, maintaining sterile conditions and assisting the surgical team within assigned duties.
example: An assistant checks that the surgeon's specified instruments and supplies are ready before a procedure.

definition: An optical power meter measures optical signal power, commonly in fiber-optic systems.
example: A technician measures received signal power at the end of a fiber link to check its loss budget.

definition: Optimization software uses mathematical algorithms to search for solutions that improve a stated objective subject to constraints.
example: A planner uses a solver to minimize staffing costs while covering every required shift.

definition: Optitex is digital design software for developing apparel patterns and simulating how garments fit and drape.
example: A pattern maker previews a jacket in three dimensions before cutting a sample.

definition: Oracle Advanced Queuing provides database-integrated message queues for asynchronous communication between applications.
example: An order service enqueues an event that a separate fulfillment process consumes.

definition: Oracle Application Framework is a Java-based framework for building web interfaces and business applications in Oracle E-Business Suite.
example: A developer extends a self-service page while retaining the application's navigation and data model.
sense_note: Often identified as OA Framework; distinguish from Oracle Application Development Framework.

definition: Oracle Application Integration Architecture provides frameworks and integration assets for connecting enterprise applications through service-oriented patterns.
example: A team uses a common message structure to exchange order data between separate applications.

definition: Oracle Autonomous Database is a managed Oracle cloud database service that automates many provisioning, maintenance and tuning tasks.
example: A team deploys a reporting database without scheduling routine patching itself.

definition: Oracle BI Answers is an Oracle Business Intelligence interface for creating ad hoc analyses against a business data model.
example: An analyst builds a sales-by-region table by selecting dimensions and measures.

definition: Oracle Business Activity Monitoring tracks business events and process metrics to support dashboards and alerts.
example: An operations manager monitors the number of orders approaching their processing deadline.

definition: Oracle Clinical is software supporting capture, management and validation of clinical study data.
example: A study data manager reviews validation findings before finalizing a dataset.

definition: Oracle Cloud is Oracle's portfolio of cloud infrastructure, platform services and applications provided remotely.
example: A team runs a database and its application on managed cloud resources.
sense_note: The label may mean the broad portfolio or Oracle Cloud Infrastructure specifically.

definition: Oracle EU Sovereign Cloud is an Oracle cloud offering designed for workloads subject to European data residency and operational sovereignty requirements.
example: An organization evaluates whether its hosting arrangement satisfies internal European residency requirements.
sense_note: No particular regulatory compliance is guaranteed solely by using the offering.

definition: Oracle Fixed Assets is an enterprise accounting module for recording, depreciating, transferring and retiring fixed assets.
example: A controller records the acquisition of equipment and runs its periodic depreciation calculation.

definition: Oracle GoldenGate is software for capturing and replicating data changes between supported systems.
example: A reporting system receives updates from an operational database without relying on periodic full copies.

definition: Oracle HRMS is an enterprise software suite for managing human resources records and related workforce processes.
example: A personnel team records a new employee's assignment and maintains their employment history.

definition: Oracle OLAP is Oracle technology for multidimensional analysis of data, including aggregation across business dimensions.
example: An analyst explores revenue totals by region, product and quarter.

definition: Oracle Primavera is a family of project management tools used for scheduling, resource planning and project controls.
example: A project planner uses a schedule to identify construction tasks on the critical path.
